title: One Word, Two GPUs: Why Gemma 4 Answers the Same Question Differently on a Laptop and a Tesla T4
why_read: A detailed, concrete debugging investigation into why identical LLM inference setups give different numeric answers across GPU architectures due to floating-point summation order.
analysis: This article traces a real and subtle bug: the same GGUF model file and llama.cpp build give different answers on a laptop GPU versus a Tesla T4, tracked down to differing numbers of processors causing different orders of floating-point addition during matrix multiplication. Because floating-point addition is not associative, splitting a big sum across 16 versus 40 processor shares changes rounding behavior and can flip the final greedy-decoded token, changing a math answer from $20 to 2000. This is a genuinely useful and specific piece of systems knowledge for anyone running local LLM inference and expecting bit-for-bit reproducibility across hardware. It's a good example of practical, hands-on investigation rather than marketing or surface-level content.
